title: Lease lattice: preemption & burst currency (PRD sketch)
content:
Status: DRAFT — exploratory concept for Dedicated capacity control plane.

Context / problem:
- Customers want predictable reserved throughput but also need occasional short bursts above committed capacity.
- Current approaches (hard reserve + ephemeral burst pools) either: (a) over-provision, (b) require manual provisioning, or (c) lead to noisy neighbor issues.
- Need a unified, operator-friendly mechanism to: allocate reserve, allow limited bursts, preempt fairly under contention, and tie to transparent economics.

Proposal summary (high level): Lease Lattice + Burst Currency
- Lease Lattice: allocate capacity as time-bound "leases" (short-lived reservations) distributed across a pool. Leases can be traded, split, or revoked with graded preemption semantics.
- Burst Currency: each customer gets a continuous balance of "burst credits" that can be spent to acquire temporary extra leases (higher QoS lane) when demand spikes. Credits accrue based on committed reservations and usage patterns (configurable accrual rules).
- Key behaviors: predictable steady-state, controlled opportunistic burst, prioritized preemption that minimizes tail-latency impact, and explicit billing for burst usage.

Goals (measurable):
- Preserve committed latency SLOs for reserved capacity >= 99.95% P99 under normal load.
- Support on-demand bursts up to 2x committed throughput for short windows (configurable) without violating isolation targets.
- Keep cost transparency: customers can see credit balance, predicted burst cost, and burn-rate.
- Provide operator controls to set global safety net thresholds and emergency quiesce.

Non-goals:
- Not attempting to fully replace Dedicated RBAC or tenancy primitives (this layers on top).
- Not a pricing rewrite; billing integration is exposed but detailed price tables postponed to follow-up design.

User stories (examples):
- As an ML platform engineer, I want my service to handle a sudden 30% traffic spike for 2 minutes without manual capacity changes.
- As product ops, I want to set a maximum daily burst spend for my team to avoid runaway bills.
- As SRE, I want predictable preemption signals so that critical low-latency routes are never evicted unexpectedly.

Core concepts (short definitions):
- Lease: time-bounded allocation on a GPU/slot (e.g., 30s–10m).
- Lease Tier / Lane: latency-aware QoS class (e.g., steady, burst, opportunistic).
- Burst Credit: integer/fractional currency; spent to acquire higher-tier leases; accrues and decays according to policy.
- Grace Window: a short period post-preempt during which requests are drained/redirected.

Design details (first pass):
1) Lease allocation lifecycle:
   - Committed path: customer's reserved pool holds long-lived leases that refresh periodically; scheduler pins these slices to avoid fragmentation.
   - Burst path: when traffic demand > reserved capacity, request layer attempts to buy temporary leases using burst credits or charged post-facto.
   - Lease reclamation: leases have soft and hard expiry. Soft-preempt: tenant notified, KV-cache kept warm for grace window. Hard-preempt: immediate reclaim and eviction.

2) Credit economics (configurable):
   - Accrual rules: e.g., 0.1 credit per minute per 1 GPU-equivalent reserved; extra accrual for underutilized commits (encourage commit+save).
   - Spend rules: cost-per-lease expressed in credits (varies by lane and lease-length).
   - Borrowing: allow negative balance to a capped debt with ramped penalty (preemption priority reduced).

3) Preemption and prioritization:
   - Multi-attribute preemptor: prioritizes by (1) SLA tier, (2) credit balance (higher balances win), (3) route criticality label, (4) age of lease.
   - Preemption signals: two-phase: notify (X sec) -> degrade lane (lower concurrency) -> evict. Integrations: tracing, logs, tenant events.

4) Safety nets and operator controls:
   - Global safety threshold: if cluster-level free capacity < T%, disable burst lane globally; fall back to queued requests or degrade model variant.
   - Emergency reserve pool: small cross-tenant pool for control-plane/troubleshooting ops.
   - Per-tenant hard caps: configured at account level (max burst concurrency, daily credit spend).

5) API and UX (surface for customers):
   - GET /v1/dedicated/credit-balance -> returns numeric balance, accrual rate, debt cap.
   - POST /v1/dedicated/burst-request {requested_extra_rps, lane, max_price_credits} -> synchronous admits or queue with partial grants.
   - Web console: realtime chart of credit-burn, predicted minutes left at current burn, "force-buy" knob for admins.

6) Observability / metrics:
   - tenant_reserved_slots, tenant_burst_slots, tenant_credit_balance, tenant_credit_accrual_rate, tenant_burst_burn_rate
   - cluster_free_capacity_pct, preempt_events_total{reason}, grace_drained_seconds_total
   - alerting: sustained negative balances, >5 preempt events/min per cluster, credit-accrual-halting anomalies.

Open implementation ideas (tradeoffs):
- Centralized vs local credit ledger: centralized ensures strong correctness (billing), local caches reduce latency but need reconciliation windows.
- Lease length tuning: longer leases reduce churn but increase fragmentation; short leases increase scheduling pressure.
- Borrowing model complexity vs fairness: allowing debt increases UX but complicates eviction fairness.

Operational runbook (sketch):
- Normal ops: autoscaler monitors reserved pool; Lease Lattice handles ephemeral bursts without escalations.
- On high contention: automatic throttles engage; operators get pager if preempt rate > threshold and cluster_free_capacity_pct < 3%.
- Capacity incident: ops can toggle global safety threshold or drain opportunistic lanes.

Billing considerations (notes):
- Credits can map to currency for invoicing; default: 1 credit ~ internal unit tied to per-lease-minute cost.
- Show predicted invoice delta before force-buy; provide tagging to map burst spend back to teams.
- Need legal review for retroactive billing if borrowing allowed.

Prototype plan (next steps):
1) Simulation sandbox (2 engineer sprint): implement scheduler sim that models leases, bursts, and preemption for synthetic tenants; measure latency/throughput outcomes.
2) Small internal pilot: carve a 1-P100 pool and run 3 internal services against Lease Lattice for 4 weeks.
3) Customer pilot: run with 1 low-risk customer (opt-in) with explicit spend cap and telemetry hooks.

Risks and mitigations:
- Complexity and edge cases in ledger reconciliation -> mitigation: bounded reconciliation window, read-repair, and conservative defaults.
- User confusion over credits -> mitigation: strong UX (balance charts), onboarding docs, and default generous accrual for first 30 days.
- Increased tail-latency during heavy preempt cycles -> mitigation: two-phase preemption + P0 lanes pinned.

Unresolved questions (to decide in follow-ups):
- Default accrual policy that balances incentive to commit vs fairness.
- How to surface cross-region credit pools and zone-local preemption.
- Billing rounding rules and dispute process for forced-buys.

TODOs (short-term):
- [ ] Draft simulation parameters (Ravi)
- [ ] Prototype credit ledger data model and API (Miguel)
- [ ] UX wireframes for console balance/buy flow (Lina)
- [ ] Legal check for borrow-and-bill model (ops/legal)

Notes / references:
- See DED-701 (old burst pool experiments) for prior telemetry.
- Related: link to "capacity-sentinel-tiling" ideas (internal notes).

Callouts for engineers:
- Keep KV cache lifecycle during soft-preempt to reduce cold-start tokens.
- Instrument lease churn metrics from day 0.

Bottom line: Lease Lattice + Burst Currency aims to give customers predictable reserved experience while enabling controlled, billable bursts. The model tries to be explicit about tradeoffs (credits -> dollars), provide operator safety knobs, and minimize surprise preemptions. This doc is a sketch — needs simulation + a small internal pilot before moving to full PRD.
